text:
maya: Heads-up — seeing unexpected S3 GETs from edge-cache service account against customer-data-prod. Appears after last night's RBAC refactor. Investigating now.
chen: On it. Can you paste a sample request-id and object key?
maya: log snippet: 
```
2026-03-19T23:12:11Z GET /customer-data-prod/objects/abc123 200 requester=arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/edge-cache-sa req_id=01-aaa
2026-03-19T23:13:02Z GET /customer-data-prod/objects/def456 200 requester=arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/edge-cache-sa req_id=01-bbb
```
Also saw this TF diff in authz-service from last night: 
```
resource "authz_mapping" "cache_workers" {
  name = "cache-workers"
-  allowed_tenants = ["internal-cache"]
+  allowed_tenants = ["internal-cache", "customer-data-prod"]
}
```
nico: That mapping change rings a bell — during the refactor we merged a couple role mappings and I think this got expanded inadvertently.
evelyn: Immediate mitigation: can we block edge-cache-sa from customer-data-prod while we triage? Temp denylist or bucket policy patch.
zack: I can push an explicit Deny on the bucket scoped to that principal while we fix the mapping. Example policy: 
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Deny",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/edge-cache-sa"},
      "Action": "s3:GetObject",
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::customer-data-prod/*"
    }
  ]
}
```
devops-bot: Deploying bucket deny patch (patch id d3f2a) to s3://customer-data-prod — initiated by zack.
devops-bot: Deploy status: SUCCESS — deny rule active.
maya: Confirming denies in logs now (requests returned 403). Good containment. We still need to rotate the edge-cache SA token and revert the mapping.
chen: Ran rotation: revoked old IAM role session tokens and updated k8s secret edge-cache/sa-creds. Commands used: 
```
aws sts revoke-session --session-id old-session-id-abc
kubectl -n infra delete secret edge-cache-sa-creds && kubectl -n infra create secret generic edge-cache-sa-creds --from-literal=token=REDACTED
```
nico: I'll open a rollback PR for the mapping and add a test to prevent tenant widening. Root cause: the merge script replaced a single-entry list with the union of lists without a change-review flag — automated merge bug. Here's the offending snippet from the merge helper: 
```
# merge_helper.py
# previously preserved explicit allowlist, new code does list.extend(other)
orig = ['internal-cache']
other = ['customer-data-prod']
# result ends up as combined, not validated
```
evelyn: Good work on containment. Please open an incident ticket (INC-) with affected object list, customer impact, timeline, and mitigation steps. We need a postmortem and a rollout policy to prevent this class of changes in RBAC.
maya: Filed INC-2026-0942 and attached logs + object keys. Also opened PR #1934 to revert authz mapping and added a unit test. Link: https://git.internal/repo/pulls/1934
zack: Suggest adding a CI gate that runs a role-binding diff check and rejects any PR that adds non-whitelisted tenant IDs to production mappings.
devops-bot: CI check on branch refactor-authz failed: role-diff-check — missing allowlist validation. Assigned to nico.
maya: Thanks everyone — containment confirmed, token rotated, rollback PR in flight. Leaving deny rule until PR merges and we validate. Will update incident page when done. :thumbsup:
